name: PB-11 | HTTP QUERY Method Injection & Anomaly Response
description: Production playbook. Ingests Wazuh alerts for rules 100200-100204 (HTTP QUERY method / RFC 10008 detections) via webhook. Extracts source IP and endpoint artifacts, enriches via AbuseIPDB, applies the composite risk_score already computed by normalize.py at detection time, then routes to automated containment or analyst escalation based on threat score threshold. Extends the signature-tuning methodology from Detection-Content to a protocol with no prior public detection content.

trigger.description: Listens for JSON payloads pushed by Wazuh ossec.conf integration block on rule IDs 100201, 100202, 100203, 100204 (group: query_method,rfc10008). Rule 100200 (missing Content-Type) is intentionally excluded - it is a protocol-compliance signal, not an attack signal, and is logged in Wazuh but not routed here.

nodes.name: Webhook Trigger
nodes.description: Entry point. Receives the JSON payload emitted by normalize.py's analyze_query_body().to_dict(), forwarded through Wazuh. All downstream nodes reference this payload via $exec.

nodes.name: Filter: Actionable Rule IDs
nodes.description: Passes only rule_id in [100201, 100202, 100203, 100204]. Rule 100200 (protocol compliance) is filtered out here as a defense-in-depth check, in addition to not being wired to the Wazuh integration block in the first place.

nodes.name: Enrich Source IP
nodes.description: Checks $exec.source_ip against AbuseIPDB. Matches the enrichment pattern already used in PB-01/02/05/06/08.

nodes.name: Apply Composite Score Routing
nodes.description: risk_score was already computed by normalize.py at detection time (see src/normalize.py compute_risk_score()). This node applies the threshold routing only - it does not recompute the score. AbuseIPDB's abuse_confidence_score from node_03 is available as supplementary context in the case notes but does not alter this routing decision, since normalize.py's score is payload-based and more specific to this attack surface than generic IP reputation.

nodes.name: Block Source IP
nodes.description: Fires only on the auto_contain branch. App target is a placeholder pending your actual containment mechanism (Wazuh active-response script vs. firewall/WAF API) - matches PB-01/PB-02's auto-contain pattern structurally, but the specific app node needs to be swapped for whatever you have wired in your Shuffle instance.

input.reason: QUERY method attack detected - rule $exec.rule_id, score $exec.risk_score

nodes.name: Create TheHive Case
nodes.description: Fires on auto_contain OR analyst_queue branches. Severity mapped from risk_score. Decoded body excerpt is truncated to 200 chars to avoid duplicating full raw payloads into TheHive - the complete body remains in Wazuh's alert store.

input.title: QUERY Method Alert - $exec.endpoint - Score $exec.risk_score
input.description: Wazuh rule $exec.rule_id fired on $exec.source_ip against $exec.endpoint. AbuseIPDB confidence: $node_03_enrich_source_ip.abuse_confidence_score. Decoded body excerpt (first 200 chars): $exec.decoded_body[:200]

nodes.name: Notify Slack
nodes.description: Channel routing mirrors PB-01/PB-09 convention: critical channel for auto-contain, general alerts channel otherwise.

input.message: QUERY method alert: rule $exec.rule_id, score $exec.risk_score, endpoint $exec.endpoint, source $exec.source_ip

IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE: This matches pb01_phishing_playbook.json's exact schema (id/name/description/tags/trigger/variables/nodes/edges structure, $exec reference pattern, {{ secrets.X }} variable convention). One node (node_05a) still has a placeholder app - swap it for whatever containment mechanism PB-01/PB-02 actually use in your Shuffle instance, since that wasn't visible in the 40-line excerpt provided. Everything else should import cleanly against your existing app configuration (abuseipdb, thehive, slack) since those app names match what's already referenced in pb01.
